summary: Obfuscated import-time Function-constructor payload injected into published tarball
details: The published tarball of @adminide-stack/forms-core@5.1.9-alpha.3 ships a lib/index.js (the package main) whose top-level content diverges from the declared source and build. src/index.ts is a 10-line re-export module and rollup.config.mjs produces plain ES re-exports, but lib/index.js prepends a ~16 KB IIFE invoked as `})(global, require);` that stashes `require` and `module` onto `global` via property names reconstructed from a custom string-shuffle routine (`spin`/`splitLane`/`peel` driven by NX/SX constant arrays), deshuffles the string "constructor" to obtain `Function` from an object reference (`Forge = peel[ctor]`), and invokes `new Function` with a deshuffled ~15 KB code body: `Forge('z', peel("[...]"))(z);`. The construct runs at import/require time with full Node capabilities (require, fs, net) available via the stashed `require`. The gap between declared source plus build config and the shipped main, combined with hand-written string deobfuscation of control identifiers and an executable payload, is the fingerprint of a payload injected into the published artifact after or outside the declared build pipeline.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
